To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hexapeptide FrcrSfa inhibits Na+/Ca2 + exchange in rat ventricular cardiomyocytes.
the hexapeptide FrcRSFa inhibits the Na+/Ca2+-exchange current (INCX) in isolated rat ventricular myocyte and that the peptide inhibits the Na+ and Ca2+ currents.
the hexapeptide FCRS Fa is a powerful inhibitor of Na+/Ca 2+ exchange in cardiac myocytes and that this inhibition is not associated with a change in the Na+ gradient across the sarcolemmal membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a new hexapeptide Frcrsfa, a fragment of the C-terminus of the Na+/Ca2+- exchanger (NCX), on Ca2+ homeostasis in rat ventricular cardiomyocytes.
the effect of the hexapeptide FrcrsfA on the Na+/Ca2+-exchange in rat ventricular myocardium.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified an inhibitor of the Na +/Ca2+ exchanger, a key regulator of Ca2+ handling in cardiomyocytes.
the Na+/Ca2+- exchanger is an attractive target for antiarrhythmic drugs.
